name: OP275
tagline: ADI's 'Butler' bipolar+JFET audio dual: China's classic 'warm, tube-like' op-amp and Musiland's house part.

lineage.note: SPICE models credited 'JCB / PMI', © ADI 1992/1995; G-grade model Rev. B dated 10/92. No PMI-branded OP275.
Sole maker, no second sources. Digi-Key labels one datasheet page 'Rochester Electronics' (aftermarket distributor).

ADI: first op-amp with this input

reputation.summary: ADI's audio dual, pitched on JFET 'sound quality'; ADI's AN-1429 says it is 'reputable with music fans'. On Soomal it is the textbook 'warm, tube-like' op-amp and Musiland's signature part (2007–2014). Soomal's RMAA plots show many low-level harmonics, possibly the source of the warmth (unproven). OEM uses include Denon DVD-A1, Yamaha DME32 and Apogee Mini-DAC.
typical_uses: Musiland (2007–2014): Long March II, Monitor, MD, HP series
Gain stage before LME49600/TPA6120 buffers (HP11, TempoTec DAII Plus)
DVD-Audio/SACD players (Denon DVD-A1, DVD-2900); HiFiMAN HM-602 filter
Pro audio: Yamaha DME32, Apogee Mini-DAC
Socket rolling in sound cards; MXR MC402 pedal (reportedly)
caveats: Needs at least ±4.5 V (9 V total); unsuited to low-voltage circuits.
Weak headphone driver alone: Soomal says it cannot drive a 300 Ω HD580 with authority.
Many low-level harmonics (Soomal RMAA); not a lowest-distortion choice by modern standards.
'Warm' is subjective and implementation-dependent; Soomal found some OP275 cards neutral.
Pricey vs NE5532/4580; Musiland later used CLC2059 (01 Mini, 2009) and MC33079 (03 US/PS, 2011).

counterfeit_notes: No confirmed counterfeit report, though a diyAudio thread alleges Chinese fakes. Its premium price (~20× an NE5532 in 2009) invites remarking. Genuine parts read 'OP275G'; check ~2–2.5 mA/amp supply current, 22 V/µs and 9 MHz. Buy OP275GPZ/GSZ from authorized distributors.

part_numbers_affected: OP275 PDIP and SOIC codes (exact list not read)
silicon_changes.identification: Not visible in the part number. Compare date or lot code with the effective date in the PCN 07_0024 Rev. E parts list.
silicon_changes.summary: Sumitomo discontinued mold compounds 6300H, 6650RL, 6710S, 6730B and 7050B, so ADI changed mold compound, and sometimes die-attach, for PDIP, SOIC and other packages, with a polyimide implementation. OP275 is linked to this PCN, but its parts-list row was not seen.
silicon_changes.audio_impact: None expected; materials only, no electrical change reported.
silicon_changes.compatibility_risk: low – die, pinout and datasheet unchanged; only materials changed.
silicon_changes.verification: Rev. E form and parts list found; no OP275 row seen, so inclusion is unconfirmed.

silicon_changes.identification: RoHS parts carry a Z suffix in the ordering code. The top mark on recent parts reads 'OP275G'.
silicon_changes.summary: Lead-free ordering codes replaced the leaded GP and GS codes. Distributors list OP275GS as obsolete and OP275GPZ/OP275GSZ as active. No die change was reported.
silicon_changes.compatibility_risk: low – new ordering code; same pinout and datasheet.
silicon_changes.verification: Based on distributor listings (Worldway, Octopart, Digi-Key).

revision_history.changes: PMI-era first edition (c. 1992–93) not found; a G-grade sheet existed by October 1992.
Pre-RoHS; lists OP275GP. Held by Futurlec and pken.net copies; changes not seen.
Reichelt copy, footer 'REV. B'. Sits between REV. A and Rev. C; changes not seen.
Current (RadioLocman; ADI component record). Date and change log not seen.
Model only: added common-mode input capacitance, corrected short-circuit current. Worst-case G grade (EOS 1.0 mV, IOS 25 nA).
Model only: corrected common-mode zero (C7 = 159.15 pF, 1 kHz vs 1.59 pF in OrCAD copy). EOS 0.5 mV, IOS 1 nA.

revision_chains.note: Unknown whether Rev. C added the lead-free Z codes. Undated mirrors may hold A or B.

open_questions: Dates of datasheet revisions A, B and C, and Rev. C's change log? Did Rev. C add the Z codes?
Is OP275 on the PCN 07_0024 Rev. E parts list, and when? Any fab or assembly PCNs?
Which revisions do undated mirrors hold (alldatasheet 49047, Octopart 9742324, datasheet4u 475420, Internet Archive 2015)?
Is 6 nV/√Hz at 1 kHz? THD+N load and frequency? Are 100 nA and 2.5 mA/amp typical or maximum?
Why does Digi-Key label OP275 'Rochester Electronics'? Who is 'JCB / PMI', and where does 'Butler' come from?

claims_confirmed: PCN 07_0024 Rev. E covers the Sumitomo mold-compound discontinuation (PDIP/SOIC mold and die-attach, polyimide); reportedly covers OP275 (https://www.analog.com/media/en/pcn/ADI_PCN_07_0024_Rev_E_Form.pdf)
Current OP275 datasheet is Revision C (https://www.radiolocman.com/datasheet/pdf.html?di=121467)
